cmu16-walk-slow.description: long-form walk derivative scaled to the admitted slow planar-speed band

variant.rationale: The exhaustive optimizer-free TRAIN-4 baseline covered all 5653 valid phases of all 28 admitted locomotion clips and found 4329 hard-safety failures. Bilateral ankle-ground impacts dominated at 3240 pair events; ankle pitch dominated hard-ROM at 807 events; ankle roll dominated velocity at 593 events; and ankle channels accounted for 317 of 339 effort-envelope events. Pre-freeze temporal/contact diagnostics confirmed that symmetric whole-clip smoothing and a contact-aware sole solve materially reduce every dominant class, while an over-strong root lock and a five-degree hip clearance are rejected because they respectively increase impacts and bilateral hip collision. This version therefore applies a symmetric low-pass trajectory solve, stronger ankle smoothing, explicit joint reserves, minimum-dwell support phases, conservative stance knee and ten-degree hip clearance, numerical stance-sole leveling, bounded swing-knee clearance, a collision-free velocity-bounded root-height majorant, and a bounded endpoint-tapered planar correction. The ankle-roll reference range extends to minus ten degrees so sole leveling can coexist with hip clearance while retaining ten degrees to the immutable hard limit; the exhaustive dynamic gate still requires zero observed hard-ROM or other hard-safety events. Stable contacts also proved that the old cmu16 nominal-a and slow crops reached the four-cycle coverage threshold only through contact chatter: nominal-a is excluded, while the slow entry is hash-bound to the longer same-split subject-16 trial-16 source and declares an 8200-basis-point planar derivative. Contact precision/recall and all retarget deltas remain ReportOnly. BodySchema hard/soft ROM, actuator, contact and safety thresholds are unchanged, and no optimizer run is authorized without fresh deterministic, kinematic, visual and exhaustive dynamic-feasibility closure.
